To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a parallel capillary electrophoretic system was developed that enables the determination of multiple small molecule analytes in parallel lanes within one microchip.
parallel separations using capillay electrophoresis (CE) on a multilanes microchip with multipexed laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) detection are demonstrated.
a multilane capillary electrophoretic chip with multiplexed detection is developed for parallel separations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a microchip electrophoresis platform for high throughput separations and the application of the platform to pKa determination.
the development of a new microchip‐based separation system that is suitable for the separation of small molecules, peptides, and proteins.

the development of a multilane capillary electrophoretic microchip with a multiplexed laser induced fluorescence detection system, and the demonstration of parallel separations using the multilane capillay electrophoretic system with multiplexed detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work has demonstrated the utility and potential for parallel separations using CE with a microchip.
the multilane CE microchip is an effective tool for the analysis of multiple samples simultaneously.
the multilane capillary electrophoretic microchip with multiplexer detection is an effective tool for high‐throughput analysis of biological samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a multilane capillary electrophoretic microchip that can be used for parallel separations and a multiplexed detection system to monitor all the channels simultaneously.
we have developed a microchip CE system that can be used to perform multiple separations in parallel and that can also be used to perform single separations in a microchip.
the multilane CE microchip with the multiplexed LID detection system is a promising tool for parallel separations of small molecule analyte mixtures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parallel separations using CE can be achieved on a multilanes microchip using a single detection system.
the multilane chip is an effective tool for parallel separations, which can be used for high throughput analysis.
the use of a multilane chip with a multiplexed detection system is a powerful tool for high‐throughput analysis.
